title: Skinned mesh disappears on second run in mobile Chrome (Web export) — fixed by forcing Vulkan ANGLE backend
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in: 4.7.1.stable

I have not yet tested earlier or development versions to determine whether this is a regression. Happy to test additional versions if it would help narrow down when this was introduced.

### System information

Editor: Godot v4.7.1.stable - Windows 10 (build 19045) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Ti (32.0.15.7270) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-13400F - exported using the Compatibility renderer (WebGL 2.0).  The bug does NOT reproduce on desktop Chrome (Windows) at all. It only reproduces on mobile Chrome (Android), and I've confirmed it is consistent across multiple different Android devices — not tied to one specific phone or GPU vendor.  On mobile Chrome, the bug's presence depends on the ANGLE graphics backend (chrome://flags/#use-angle):  Default (OpenGL ES) → bug reproduces (skinned mesh invisible) Vulkan → bug does not reproduce (skinned mesh renders correctly)

### Issue description

I'm seeing the same skinned mesh disappearance issue described in this thread, and I've isolated a new data point that may help narrow down the root cause: on mobile Chrome (Android), forcing the Vulkan ANGLE backend instead of the default OpenGL ES backend fixes the issue. This strongly suggests the bug lives in how the Compatibility (WebGL2/GLES3) renderer's skeleton bone-matrix texture is uploaded/cached, and that the OpenGL ES ANGLE translation layer on Android is mishandling it (likely a texture cache invalidation issue).

A MeshInstance3D with a Skeleton3D and an AnimationPlayer renders correctly on first load, but becomes invisible on subsequent runs. The mesh is still present in the scene tree, transforms are valid, visible is true, and no errors are printed to the console — the mesh simply stops being drawn. This is mobile-Chrome-specific; I cannot reproduce it on desktop Chrome under any ANGLE backend, only on Android.

New finding: ANGLE backend matters on mobile

On mobile Chrome (Android), I can reliably toggle the bug on and off by changing the ANGLE graphics backend via chrome://flags/#use-angle:

Default (OpenGL ES) → bug reproduces (skinned mesh invisible)
Vulkan → bug does not reproduce (skinned mesh renders correctly, including across reloads)

I've confirmed this is consistent across multiple different Android devices, so it doesn't appear to be tied to a specific phone model or GPU vendor — it looks like a general issue with how the Compatibility renderer's skeleton texture is handled under Android's default (non-Vulkan) ANGLE path.

I tried the following workarounds without success: expanding custom_aabb on the MeshInstance3D, and calling Skeleton3D.reset_bone_poses() deferred in _ready(). This affects a game deployed on CrazyGames.

### Steps to reproduce

Create a scene with a skinned character (Skeleton3D + MeshInstance3D with a Skin + AnimationPlayer).
Export for Web using the Compatibility renderer.
Serve the build and open it in Chrome on an Android device (default ANGLE backend, OpenGL ES).
Close the tab/app and reopen the build — the skinned mesh is no longer visible.
On the same device, go to chrome://flags/#use-angle, set it to Vulkan, relaunch Chrome, and repeat steps 3-4 — the mesh now renders correctly and stays visible across reloads.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

I can prepare a minimal reproduction project if needed.
